references.text: The Lord did not choose Israel because they were a great people, but because of his love and his promise to the fathers. This emphasizes that the land promise was not based on Israel's own merit.

Just before verse 6, Moses warns Israel against believing that their righteousness is the reason they receive the land. God drives out the nations because of their wickedness and to fulfill the promise to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
Moses describes Israel as stubborn and rebellious, which confirms the description of them as a stiff-necked people.
The Lord calls Israel a stiff-necked people after the sin of the golden calf, which is the same characterization used in Deuteronomy 9:6.
The Lord repeats that Israel is a stiff-necked people and therefore refuses to go with them himself.
The Lord again describes Israel as a stiff-necked people in connection with the renewal of the covenant.
Paul explains that righteousness does not come from works, but through faith and grace. This aligns with the fact that Israel did not receive the land because of their own righteousness.
God's election is not based on works, but on his own purpose. This supports the idea that Israel did not deserve the land through their righteousness.
Salvation is by grace through faith, not by works. This reflects the principle that Israel did not receive the land by their own righteousness.
God saved us not because of righteous deeds we had done, but according to his mercy. This confirms that God's gifts are not based on human merit.
